Hi Carla — thanks for the clear set of scenarios. Happy to map this out. High-level answers below; I pasted a short matrix to the attachments and can hop on a call if you'd like to walk through it.

1) Entitlements on downgrade: 
- KV cache persistency: we can offer 30 days of cache persistence after downgrade as a default for pilots (this keeps your warm starts but we do reclaim memory if you exceed the new cap).
- Model-pin guarantees: we can provide a 30-day pin; after that we revert to the pinned-model class but not the exact hash unless paid retention is active.
- Feature flags (A/B tool calling, streaming): retained for 60 days but streaming SLOs are subject to capacity class.

2) Discounts / credits: 
- If you commit and then reduce on a prorated basis within the same billing cycle, we issue a one-time credit equal to the difference between committed spend and actual usage, capped at 50% of the original commit in pilot scenarios.
- We avoid retroactive discounting across previous billing cycles unless there's an approved exec exception.

3) Quantization / model variants: 
- Model builds that are deployed to dedicated pools can be rolled back within 14 days. After 14 days we recommend a rebuild to ensure kernel-opt compatibility; we can lock a variant for 30 days with a small retention fee.

I've attached a simple "escape routes" matrix and a proposed MAP for the pilot that lays out triggers and triggers-to-actions. Ben — looping you in for pricing flexibility and any standard concession guardrails.

Best,
Priyom Das

Thanks Priyom — +1 on the matrix. A few pricing notes for Augment.ai: 

- For pilot commitments <= $50k ARR equivalent, standard concession is a 10% one-time onboarding credit plus a soft-commit discount of 7% for the pilot month.
- If they commit to a three-month ramp (tiered commit), we can structure a 12% entry discount with a 6% grace credit on downgrade within the first 45 days.
- We'll avoid hard discounts beyond 15% without a finance approval. Any exception we should route to the revenue ops queue with the deal_id (AUG-2027-0421).

Monica — if they ask for model-pin longer than 30 days, what's the retention fee we typically recommend?

Ben — recommend $500/mo per pinned-model retention (up to 3 models) for pilot customers; beyond that we move to a usage-based retention fee that scales with vGPU hours. Rationale: we need a cover for kernel compatibility maintenance and storage reservation.

Also, for the 30-day cache persistence, add a soft throttle policy after day 21 if their retention hits >70% of their downgraded bucket — we don't want to starve other customers. Priyom, I'll add the throttle language to the attachment and update the MAP.
